intro.data: You have THREE uniform conversions in a row: safeHead turns a List into an Optional, 'As a List' turns that Optional into a thin List, and safeHead again turns it back into an Optional. Run all three in order and you get a SINGLE conversion, List ⇒ Optional — that's vertical composition of three transformations. At each type its component is the three component arrows composed: (γ·β·α)_A = γ_A ∘ β_A ∘ α_A. Pick that triple composite at each type; the look-alikes splice in a default and aren't natural.
intro.alchemy: You have THREE uniform methods in a row: F to G, then G to H, then H to K. Run all three and you get a SINGLE method, F ⇒ K — vertical composition of three. At each material its component is the three steps composed: (γ·β·α)_A = γ_A ∘ β_A ∘ α_A. Pick that triple composite; the look-alikes splice in a spare and aren't natural.
intro.spellcraft: You have THREE uniform workings in a row: F to G, then G to H, then H to K. Cast all three and you get a SINGLE working, F ⇒ K — vertical composition of three. At each essence its component is the three runes composed: (γ·β·α)_A = γ_A ∘ β_A ∘ α_A. Choose that triple composite; the look-alikes splice in a conjured one and aren't natural.
intro.abstract: Given α : F ⇒ G, β : G ⇒ H and γ : H ⇒ K, build the vertical composite γ·β·α : F ⇒ K. Its component at A is γ_A ∘ β_A ∘ α_A. Pick that composite at each object; non-composite, non-natural families are offered as distractors.

afterSuccess.data: You stacked THREE conversions into one: safeHead (List⇒Optional), then 'As a List' (Optional⇒List), then safeHead again (List⇒Optional) — a single List⇒Optional conversion whose component at each type is the three component arrows composed, (γ·β·α)_A = γ_A ∘ β_A ∘ α_A. The 'Default Triple' and 'Drop-the-Middle' families spliced in a default and broke the square. Natural transformations compose, however many you stack.
afterSuccess.alchemy: You stacked THREE methods into one: F⇒G, G⇒H, H⇒K give a single F⇒K method, its component the three steps composed — (γ·β·α)_A = γ_A ∘ β_A ∘ α_A. The spare-splicing and middle-dropping families broke the square.
afterSuccess.spellcraft: You stacked THREE workings into one: F⇒G, G⇒H, H⇒K give a single F⇒K working, its component the three runes composed — (γ·β·α)_A = γ_A ∘ β_A ∘ α_A. The conjuring and middle-dropping families broke the square.
afterSuccess.abstract: γ·β·α : F ⇒ K is natural, with (γ·β·α)_A = γ_A ∘ β_A ∘ α_A; the non-composite families fail naturality. Vertical composition is associative, so stacking three (or any number of) natural transformations again yields a natural transformation.

reveal.summary: Vertical composition stacks any number of natural transformations. If α : F ⇒ G, β : G ⇒ H and γ : H ⇒ K, then γ·β·α : F ⇒ K is natural, with component (γ·β·α)_A = γ_A ∘ β_A ∘ α_A at each object. Associativity means the grouping does not matter.
reveal.programmerAnalogy: Chaining three polymorphic conversions: (xs => safeHead(xs)) then (o => o.toList()) then (ys => safeHead(ys)).
